A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VisJudge-Bench research. Their complete 62-page contents, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations in Table 3, annotation analyses in Appendix A, scaling experiments and downstream results for MatPlotAgent and HAIChart.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark evaluations, annotation analyses, scaling experiments and downstream application results.

M1.justification: Both retain the same adaptive rubric generation, annotation pipeline, four model backbones and GRPO/LoRA training with the same composite reward. Removing the prose reference to adaptive score weights does not establish a procedural change: Appendix C retains identical scoring prompts and six-score averaging.

E1.justification: Both use the same 3,090 visualizations across three categories and 32 subtypes, plus the same MatPlotAgent generation and HAIChart recommendation evaluations on VizML. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same 12 baseline MLLMs and four VisJudge variants. The MatPlotAgent and HAIChart comparisons retain the same baseline, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-72B and VisJudge conditions.

E3.justification: The train/validation/test counts, training budgets, inference settings, evaluation metrics and downstream protocols remain unchanged. Appendix B.6 newly documents selection of an existing error-analysis subset; its retained sample counts and findings do not establish a changed experiment.

E4.justification: The scaling analysis moves from v2 Section 5.3 to v3 Appendix E.1 with its experiment and findings retained. Complexity comparisons, annotation analyses, cross-architecture analyses and Appendix B case studies also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report three inference runs per model and averaging of their outputs. Annotation dispersion and consistency reporting are retained, with no added seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The shortened Section 5.2.1 omits explicit cross-model mean MAEs for Fidelity (1.006), Insight Discovery (0.883) and Semantic Readability (0.991). This is a limited reduction in reported summaries: the underlying Table 3 entries, downstream tables, plotted results and case-study scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 retains the same exponential accuracy-reward equation, reward weights and format-reward definition. Its wording clarification adds no mathematical reasoning, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, claimed gap in general MLLM assessment and benefits of specialized training. The headline 23.9% MAE reduction and 60.5% correlation improvement over GPT-5 are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7 explicitly identifies point-estimate scoring as a limitation for representing diverse human preferences and states that missing raw data limits fidelity verification. v2 already discussed visual-only assessment and distribution-based future work, so these are limited clarifications of applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix B.6 adds the selection criterion for the existing 139 multi-visualization and 94 dashboard cases: at least one model has absolute score deviation above 1.0. The new Reproducibility Statement specifies dataset contents at the existing repository. Conversely, v3 removes the exact ImageFilter.FIND_EDGES implementation reference and the explicit commitment to release trained model weights; the PDFs do not establish an actual change in resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds supporting citations including LEAD, DeepEye-SQL, the data-agent survey and automated GUI testing, and replaces the generic CloudResearch citation with Hartman et al. (2023). These additions do not substantially alter the retained positioning relative to aesthetic assessment, chart understanding and visualization evaluation.

P1.justification: v3 condenses related-work and experimental-analysis paragraphs, rewrites the limitations, adds reproducibility and acknowledgment sections, and moves the scaling subsection into Appendix E. Terminology, grammar, bibliography entries and cross-references receive limited cleanup; the overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: All 27 figures and eight tables are retained. The scaling plot moves from main-text Figure 8 to Appendix Figure 27, other displays reflow, and conference headers are added. The annotation-interface illustration receives a small text correction without changing its substantive content.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency by explaining the previously unspecified error-subset selection in Appendix B.6 and making scoring limitations explicit. Its reproducibility statement and editorial cleanup improve navigation while preserving the experimental evidence. Removing the edge-detector detail and explicit model-weight-release commitment weakens some documentation, but the clarification of how the error analysis was selected provides a limited net quality gain.
